characters.description: A formidable independent cultivator whose incomplete body cultivation is steadily destroying him. He and Falling Leaf search the wilderness for a manual that may complete his training and halt the fatal decline.
characters.name: Sen

characters.description: Sen's Ghost Panther companion, chosen family, and hunting partner. She can pass for human and fights powerful spirit beasts beside him. She recognizes that his incomplete cultivation is killing him but remains committed to staying with him.
characters.name: Falling Leaf

characters.description: One of Sen’s established teachers and protectors. Feng has repeatedly helped restrain Sen’s most dangerous training impulses.
characters.name: Feng

characters.description: A senior cultivator counted among Sen’s established teachers and protectors. Kho previously helped restrain Sen’s dangerous approach to training.
characters.name: Kho

characters.description: One of Sen's teachers and a trusted provider of alchemical aid. She previously helped restrain his dangerous approach to training, and her medicines remain among the limited resources available to him and Falling Leaf during their search.
characters.name: Caihong

characters.description: The elusive cultivator Sen has been seeking and the holder of the Five-Fold Body Transformation Manual. Her apparent madness is a performance. After saving Sen, she offers access to the manual in return for five years in which he will serve her or submit to her observation.
characters.name: Nascent-soul alchemist

characters.description: A powerful cultivator whom Falling Leaf names as part of her chosen family.
characters.name: Feng Ming

characters.description: An evolved Ghost Panther who approaches Sen and Falling Leaf after secretly observing them. He claims authority as a surviving pride father and demands that Falling Leaf join a wider conflict involving their kind, placing lineage against the family she has chosen.
characters.name: Elder Ghost Panther

characters.description: A confident cultivator who reaches the defenses around Sen’s camp and shows interest in Sen and Falling Leaf. Sen drives him away but suspects that he remains nearby.
characters.name: Camp visitor

characters.description: The self-aware leader of a vast spider colony. She attacks Sen's fortified camp to avenge spiders he killed while rescuing the poisoned Falling Leaf, directing thousands of her offspring against his formations and making the conflict personally charged.
characters.name: Spider matriarch

characters.description: A self-aware young dragon and the strongest creature Sen has directly fought. It takes part in a coordinated spirit-beast assault against Sen and Falling Leaf. Sen kills it, but the battle leaves him severely wounded and almost without qi, while whoever organized the attack remains unknown.
characters.name: Dragon

characters.description: A powerful being from Sen's earlier travels whose unfinished business now requires another meeting. Once his health is restored, Sen decides to seek the turtle on his own schedule rather than risk it appearing at a more dangerous or disruptive time.
characters.name: Ancient divine turtle

characters.description: A royal cultivator and former associate whom Sen expects may confront him during his planned stop in the capital. He wants to avoid both her and a fight, yet regards the possibility as serious enough to admit that he may have to kill her if no alternative remains.
characters.name: Royal princess

characters.description: Sen's former companion and capital contact, whose protected house he visits quietly after a long absence.
characters.name: Former companion

characters.description: An independent artisan outside the capital who supplies formation flags without the institutional obligations Sen wants to avoid. He sells Sen a usable replacement set, accepts a commission for specialized flags, and sees an opportunity in Sen's alchemical skill.
characters.name: Formation-maker

characters.description: A protective former travelling companion of Sen and an ally in the capital. After the princess's failed assault, she confronts the royal cultivator, explains the mortal danger that forced Sen to leave, and insists that any future dealings with him must not endanger him.
characters.name: Feng's watcher

characters.description: A male Ghost Panther who has demanded that Falling Leaf accompany him. Falling Leaf personally refused, with Sen supporting her choice. Sen nevertheless expects the claimant to return, leaving another unresolved challenge to her autonomy.
characters.name: Ghost Panther claimant

characters.description: A capable stranger who bypasses Sen's camp formations and says an unnamed master sent him with a proposal. He appears close to Sen's cultivation level and presses for a hearing despite Sen's firm refusal to accept another unknown obligation.
characters.name: Messenger

characters.description: Three junior disciples who block Sen's path, demand recognition of their sect and honor, and prepare to attack him. Sen overwhelms them with Heaven's Shadow, an apparently nonlethal technique whose lasting effects are not yet known.
characters.name: Three junior disciples

characters.description: An inner disciple sent to locate three missing juniors. She believes the assignment may be retaliation from an elder whose advances she rejected. Finding the disciples alive but psychologically devastated, she puts their immediate survival ahead of reporting to her sect.
characters.name: Core-stage investigator

characters.description: A returning sea captain who recognizes Sen, cites an earlier debt, and agrees to carry him to the ancient divine turtle cove.
characters.name: Returning sea captain

recaps.ending: Sen reaches the coast alone and accepts that he can no longer return to an anonymous wandering life. Wearing Caihong's blue robes and openly using the name Lu Sen, he books passage with a captain who carried him before. Two admiring sect siblings approach him before departure. Instead of encouraging their fascination with Judgment's Gale, he corrects their exaggerated stories, warns them that his path has brought pain, and gives them healing elixirs to use for others. He then sails for the ancient divine turtle's cove. Falling Leaf remains voluntarily with the nascent-soul alchemist to train with weapons, and her bond with Sen is intact. The alchemist still holds the remainder of Sen's five-year obligation even though he now possesses the manual. The royal princess is alive in the former companion's care, the formation commission remains pending, and the Ghost Panther claims on Falling Leaf are unsettled. Three cultivators struck by Heaven's Shadow remain severely traumatized under a core-stage investigator's care, creating a possible conflict with their sect that Sen does not yet know about.
recaps.in_short: Sen begins the volume close to death because his incomplete body cultivation is destroying him. He and Falling Leaf find the nascent-soul alchemist who owns the Five-Fold Body Transformation Manual, but she demands five years of service or observation. After retrieving rare mushrooms, surviving attacks, and discovering his unusual pill-refining method, Sen makes the dangerously potent pill required for his transformation and survives. He receives the manual, gains another core layer, and leaves Falling Leaf training with the alchemist while he visits the capital and then heads for the ancient divine turtle. In the capital he defeats the royal princess without killing her and arranges for formation supplies. On the road, an unwanted messenger and a plague-stricken village force him to reconsider his reflexive hostility. His new Heaven's Shadow technique spares three attackers but leaves them catastrophically impaired. Sen accepts the public identity he had tried to evade and sails toward the turtle's cove, while his debt to the alchemist, the Ghost Panther dispute, and possible sect retaliation remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Sen became an independent cultivator known publicly as Judgment's Gale, combining body cultivation, unusual qi abilities, and exceptional alchemical talent. Feng, Kho, and Caihong became his teachers and senior protectors, repeatedly restraining the most dangerous extremes of his training. Falling Leaf, a Ghost Panther able to pass for human, chose Sen and those teachers as her family and travelled beside him as both companion and hunting partner. Their bond is chosen family rather than simple convenience. Sen also formed ties in the capital, including a former companion who can relay messages and a royal princess whose relationship with him became strained. His earlier travels created unfinished business with an ancient divine turtle.

Sen and Falling Leaf search the wilderness for the Five-Fold Body Transformation Manual while his condition steadily deteriorates. Rest, liquid qi, and healing elixirs offer less relief as the tissues of his body begin to fail. Falling Leaf refuses to abandon him, and Sen refuses to divide the search because he will not expose her to danger alone. After months without success, a tide of spirit beasts attacks their fortified shelter. Sen, barely able to stand, unleashes a devastating qi technique to protect Falling Leaf and collapses. He awakens healed and separated from her in the home of the cultivator they sought. The supposedly mad nascent-soul cultivator reveals that her behavior was deliberate and confirms that she owns the manual. She saved Sen partly because she fears Feng's response to his death. Sen accepts her price: five years of service or observation in exchange for access to the manual. He refuses to include Falling Leaf in the obligation, though she may stay or leave and must protect the cultivator's secrecy.

The nascent-soul cultivator delays giving Sen the manual until he has recovered. Over several months he regains much of his strength, though he remains below his former physical condition. She tests his ability to manage several kinds of qi and then sends him to retrieve three superior air-attributed dusk mushrooms from a mountain, allowing only three months. Falling Leaf accompanies him. On the road, Sen hears distorted stories about Judgment's Gale and later confirms that the feared name belongs to him after a conflict with Swift River cultivators. He and Falling Leaf initially spare and disarm four attackers. When their sect sends pursuit, Sen kills the leader but gives the survivors a face-saving account that may prevent escalation. Near the mountain, an elder Ghost Panther secretly observes the pair and then claims authority over Falling Leaf, demanding that she join a wider conflict among their kind. Falling Leaf rejects lineage as a basis for obedience. She names Sen, Feng Ming, Kho, and Caihong as her chosen pride. Sen prepares to resist, and the elder withdraws, leaving the larger Ghost Panther crisis unresolved.

Sen and Falling Leaf continue up the mountain under near-constant attack. An intrusive sect-affiliated cultivator follows them, claims superior cultivation and knowledge of Sen's past, but refuses to explain his purpose. Sen drives him away without killing him. The pair then finds the concealed hollow containing the dusk mushrooms. A giant spider poisons Falling Leaf, and Sen burns through the colony to carry her out and treat her with one of Caihong's healing pills. While Falling Leaf remains unconscious, a self-aware spider matriarch leads thousands against Sen's fortified camp to avenge her colony. Sen demonstrates overwhelming force but permits the survivors to retreat. Falling Leaf recovers fully, and the pair begins the return journey with the required mushrooms. They help a village by killing its bandit tormentors, and Falling Leaf agrees that they might someday live near ordinary people so she can learn their ways at her own pace. Before reaching safety, a coordinated force of spirit beasts attacks, including a young dragon. Sen kills the dragon and destroys the attackers, but is badly wounded and nearly emptied of qi. He and Falling Leaf recover in hiding, unable to identify who organized the assault.

Sen and Falling Leaf return after three months with the dusk mushrooms. The nascent-soul alchemist orders Sen to make a pill from them, only to discover that he has never learned conventional pill refining and has always made elixirs in an ordinary pot. His elixirs prove unusually good, but he repeatedly fails at even the simplest pill despite following the primer correctly. The alchemist suspends his deadline and joins the investigation. After hundreds of failed variations, Sen recognizes that his relief at leaving the workshop has hurt her. He finds her a rare ice-qi lotus, explains that he wanted distance from failure rather than from her, and repairs their working relationship. Falling Leaf also becomes more independent, visiting a town alone and matching Sen in a demanding spar. Sen finally abandons rigid recipe execution and applies the responsive intuition he uses for elixirs. This produces a successful healing pill. Repeated attempts confirm both the breakthrough and a new danger: his pills are consistently much stronger than intended. Because the Five-Fold Body Transformation requires Sen to make his own exacting pills, he must learn to reduce their potency before risking the process. The alchemist also agrees to find suitable training for Falling Leaf.

Sen cannot make his pills reliably weaker, and the stabilization holding his damaged body together begins to fail. With perhaps only weeks left, he stops experimenting and rushes through the remaining primer. He completes its final, exceptionally difficult pill and collapses. The nascent-soul alchemist then confirms that this dangerously potent result is the actual pill needed for the Five-Fold Body Transformation and gives him only even odds of survival. Falling Leaf's certainty that he will live gives Sen the resolve to proceed. Away from the shelter, the pill tears down and rebuilds his body. Sen remains conscious through sword practice and his trust in Falling Leaf, completes the transformation, and survives without a heavenly tribulation. His new strength and speed greatly exceed his old limits, though he needs time to control them. The alchemist finally gives him the manual, and he makes copies with the long-term hope of widening access. His five-year obligation to her remains in force. Sen decides to travel to the ancient divine turtle, stopping first in the capital. Falling Leaf chooses to remain with the alchemist for weapon training. Before leaving alone, Sen also forms another layer of his core without a tribulation.

Sen enters the capital quietly and visits his former companion after two years without word. She is angry at his silence but relieved that he survived, and tells him that both the royal princess and the earlier sect-affiliated visitor have been seeking information about him. Sen asks her to pass messages to Feng, Kho, and Caihong. The princess then arrives with six cultivators. Sen kills the most aggressive attacker, frightens the unwilling participants away, and refuses to kill them once they abandon the fight. The princess accuses him of murdering her father and attacks. Sen denies the act, avoids her strikes, and disarms her without injury when her rage threatens civilians. He leaves her alive in his former companion's care. Sen purchases temporary formation flags from an independent artisan and commissions specialized replacements, offering future alchemical help and advancement aids in exchange for supplies and possible instruction. Feng's watcher confronts the princess and warns her against another attack. She later drives away an unwanted visitor, offers to accompany Sen, and accepts his message for Feng. Sen strengthens the formations protecting her home, declines her offer, and departs south alone before the capital's powerful factions can impose new obligations.

On the road south, a messenger bypasses Sen’s formations and presses an unnamed master’s proposal. Sen refuses to hear it, and the encounter becomes a duel. The messenger is a skilled body cultivator and swordsman, but Sen defeats and spares him. The man follows for two days demanding an honorable death until Sen rejects his idea of honor as an excuse for further violence. Their dispute pauses when Sen finds a village devastated by disease. Most residents are already beyond recovery, so Sen tends the dying, burns bodies, and offers relief while saving only three young villagers. The messenger helps under his direction and admits that his master’s need cannot compare with this suffering. After a week, Sen leaves the six survivors and resumes his journey alone. Grief changes his outlook: he rejects both reflexive hostility and unguarded trust. When three cultivators threaten him, he creates Heaven’s Shadow, a nonlethal sword technique that forces them to experience emotions they have suppressed. Later, a core-stage investigator finds all three alive but catastrophically traumatized beneath the snow. She moves them to safety and may have to report a technique whose source witnesses regard as inhuman. Sen remains unaware of the possible conflict with her sect.

As Sen nears the coast, ordinary towns help him regain emotional balance after the plague village. He accepts that his sorrow will remain and decides to approach future strangers with wary judgment instead of automatic hostility. He also abandons the hope of returning to an uncomplicated, anonymous life. Wearing the blue robes Caihong gave him, he openly accepts the identity and reputation he once tried to avoid. At the harbor, Sen finds a captain and crew who carried him before and arranges passage to the ancient divine turtle's cove. Before departure, two young sect siblings follow him because they admire the stories surrounding Judgment's Gale. Sen corrects the exaggerated tales and explains that his achievements have also brought pain. He gives each sibling a high-quality healing elixir, encouraging them to help others rather than imitate his violence. Sen then boards the ship and sails toward his appointment with the turtle. Falling Leaf remains by choice with the nascent-soul alchemist for weapon training. Sen still owes the alchemist the balance of their five-year bargain, and the Ghost Panther dispute remains open. He does not know that Heaven's Shadow has left three cultivators severely impaired or that their sect may respond.

characters.description: An independent cultivator and disciple of Feng Ming whose newly intensified anger is disrupting both his judgment and his cultivation. He travels with Falling Leaf, Feng's watcher, and a reluctant fire cultivator while trying to understand the danger within himself.
characters.name: Sen

characters.description: Sen's transformed Ghost Panther companion and chosen family.
characters.name: Falling Leaf

characters.description: A powerful cultivator who taught Sen and assigned a covert protector to watch over him. Though absent from the journey, Feng Ming remains one of Sen's established teachers and protectors. His past guidance continues to shape both Sen's training and the company around him.
characters.name: Feng Ming

characters.description: One of Sen's senior teachers and powerful protectors. His likely response to serious harm against Sen is enough to make informed enemies cautious. Although he remains offstage as the journey begins, his connection to Sen is an important part of the young cultivator's protection.
characters.name: Kho Jaw-Long

characters.description: Sen's formidable teacher and a nascent-soul cultivator who has recently reunited with him.
characters.name: Caihong

characters.description: A late-core covert cultivator assigned by Feng to protect Sen. She continues travelling with him, although he distrusts her after she manipulated him in an attempt to reach her estranged brother. Even so, he listens when she warns that his growing anger poses an urgent danger.
characters.name: Feng's watcher

characters.description: A lazy and vocal fire cultivator sent to travel with Sen under an agreement with the Order's matriarch. His reluctance and complaints repeatedly test Sen's already unstable temper. Sen gives him the choice to stop complaining or leave the group.
characters.name: Reluctant fire cultivator

characters.description: A Clear Spring core cultivator who previously sparred with Sen. She recognizes him when his party arrives, while she and Falling Leaf immediately regard each other with suspicion.
characters.name: Clear Spring core cultivator

characters.description: The Clear Spring cultivator travelling near Sen is revealed as a princess when capital officials recognize her. Facing a forced marriage to a dangerous noble, she gains Sen's conditional help while offering a possible route to the manual he needs.
characters.name: Princess

characters.description: The elusive leader of Clear Spring, powerful enough that Sen cannot sense his cultivation. He tests Sen's restraint and explains that the sect possesses the needed manual but cannot access it.
characters.name: Clear Spring patriarch

characters.description: A Clear Spring water cultivator protected within the sect by his family's status. Sen will not hunt him, but intends to answer any attack with lethal force.
characters.name: Hostile Clear Spring cultivator

characters.description: An ancient, aware body of water that communicates through qi and images. It broadens Sen's understanding of water and warns that merely confining his anger may leave his heart permanently hardened. It shelters him when its first attempt to share knowledge overwhelms him.
characters.name: Clear Spring

characters.description: The founder of a cult that holds people inside a protected compound. When Caihong breaks its defenses, he orders his followers to resist and tries to escape. His authority collapses as the compound's formation fails and Caihong acts to recover those held there on Sen's behalf.
characters.name: Temple of Eternity's Edge leader

characters.description: An ancient divine turtle whose guidance placed Sen on the Five-Fold Body Transformation path. Its intervention is the reason Sen began the incomplete body-cultivation method whose manual he now seeks.
characters.name: Ancient divine turtle

characters.description: An overwhelmingly powerful dragon concealed within a deliberately barren wilderness. He suppresses Sen and Falling Leaf with ease, excludes Falling Leaf from the confrontation, and declares that Sen must learn before dying.
characters.name: Wind dragon

characters.description: The leader of a spirit ox herd that shelters Sen and Falling Leaf while his injured leg heals. She explains why spirit beasts follow Sen and directs him toward a barren western region where he may find resolution or death.
characters.name: Spirit ox herd mother

characters.description: The princess's politically cautious brother. A diviner has warned him that Sen's arrival could bring either fortune or disaster, so he approaches Sen seeking peaceful relations rather than an immediate favor.
characters.name: Noble prince

characters.description: The royal father who approved the princess's unwanted marriage to Choi Zhi Peng. His decision leaves the prince looking for another way to prevent the wedding.
characters.name: King

characters.description: The royal mother who, with the king, approved the princess's unwanted marriage to Choi Zhi Peng.
characters.name: Queen

characters.description: A competing royal heir who attacks the prince during the palace confrontation, turning the exposure of the king into an immediate struggle for the throne. His intervention forces the prince to defend both his life and his claim to rule while the royal household is in crisis.
characters.name: Rival royal brother

characters.description: The House of Choi heir selected as the princess's husband. He is a powerful and cruel noble, and the arranged match places the princess at the center of a dangerous conflict between the royal family and a great house.
characters.name: Choi Zhi Peng

characters.description: A nascent-soul leader of the Steel Griffin sect who intervenes after one of its elders attacks Sen and Falling Leaf. Revealed as Feng's brother, he accepts severe punishment for the elder to prevent a wider conflict.
characters.name: Steel Griffin leader

characters.description: A Steel Griffin elder who attempts to intimidate Sen and Falling Leaf. When she prepares to attack, Sen suppresses and wounds her.
characters.name: Steel Griffin elder

characters.description: The bearded nascent-soul leader behind the Shadow Eagle Talon Syndicate. His long-range assault devastates part of the city while pursuing Sen's group, establishing him as a threat far beyond Sen's cultivation stage.
characters.name: Shadow Eagle Talon Syndicate head

characters.description: A nascent-soul sect leader and influential city power. She joins other senior cultivators in restraining the Syndicate head and supports Sen's campaign because she regards the criminal organization as a danger to the capital.
characters.name: Golden Phoenix matriarch

characters.description: A dangerous and elusive nascent-soul cultivator who may possess the final known copy of the Five-Fold Body Transformation Manual. Locating her becomes Sen's remaining lead after the capital search fails.
characters.name: Mad nascent-soul cultivator

recaps.ending: Sen breaks the power of the Shadow Eagle Talon Syndicate and kills its nascent-soul head with a prepared poison trap. He then removes Choi Zhi Peng and forces the king to confess to trafficking people to demonic cultivators and abusing and murdering boys. The prince kills his father and an attacking brother, takes the throne, and receives quiet support from two senior sect powers. The princess is free from the marriage but rejects Sen because of his coercive intervention and the trauma it caused. The queen is imprisoned. Sen apologizes to the new king and to Feng's watcher for manipulating others while claiming moral certainty. He releases the watcher from Feng's assignment and leaves her in the capital with the fire cultivator, a fortified house, and an elixir for his advancement. Falling Leaf chooses to accompany Sen into the northwestern wilderness. They depart to find a dangerous nascent-soul cultivator who may hold the only remaining lead to the manual needed to prevent Sen's incomplete body transformation from killing him.
recaps.in_short: Sen seeks the Five-Fold Body Transformation Manual while worsening anger threatens his judgment. Clear Spring cannot release its sealed copy, and a dragon purges the heart demon driving Sen toward violence and self-destruction. In the capital, Sen agrees to help a princess escape marriage to Choi Zhi Peng, survives sect attacks, forms an abnormal second core layer, and wages war on the Shadow Eagle Talon Syndicate. Golden Phoenix has no manual, so Sen poisons the Syndicate's nascent-soul head, exposes Choi's cruelty, and forces the king to confess grave crimes. The prince kills the king and a rival brother and becomes ruler, while the princess rejects Sen for engineering the confrontation. Sen releases Feng's watcher from duty and leaves her with the improving fire cultivator. With the new king quietly supported by senior sect leaders, Sen and Falling Leaf depart for the northwestern wilderness to seek a mad nascent-soul cultivator and the last credible manual lead.

recaps.text: Previously: Sen became an independent cultivator under the guidance of Feng Ming, Kho Jaw-Long, and Caihong. Falling Leaf, a Ghost Panther transformed into human form, became his travelling companion and chosen family. Sen's unusual cultivation and readiness to protect those close to him earned him formidable enemies as well as a dangerous reputation. Feng assigned a covert cultivator to watch over him, but her manipulation of Sen in pursuit of her estranged brother damaged their trust. As this volume begins, Sen travels with Falling Leaf, the watcher, and a reluctant fire cultivator sent under an Order agreement. His teachers remain powerful offstage protectors, but Sen must make his own decisions about the threats ahead.

Sen's anger has intensified since forming his core. After repeated spirit-beast attacks, he threatens war against the bear-cat beasts, alarming Falling Leaf and the rest of the party. Falling Leaf also warns that his unfinished Five-Fold Body Transformation is dangerous without its manual. At Clear Spring, Sen discovers that the sect possesses the manual but cannot retrieve it from a time-accelerated room sealed from within. The sect patriarch instead asks him to spend time with the sentient spring. Sen gains a broader understanding of water qi and large, interdependent techniques, but the spring warns that he is confining his anger rather than resolving it. If he continues, that anger may become a permanent part of him. His search remains urgent, and the inaccessible manual means he must continue toward the capital.

A hostile Clear Spring cultivator hires professionals to cripple Sen. Sen defeats them, but the patriarch refuses to pursue the noble patron because of his family, destroying Sen's trust in the sect. Elsewhere, Caihong breaks the defenses of the Temple of Eternity's Edge, kills its fleeing leader, and ends the cult's control of its captives. Sen resumes his northern journey. A Clear Spring core cultivator follows the party and eventually admits that she wants Sen's help with a dangerous noble-family problem. She claims her family may be able to obtain the manual, but Sen refuses to risk his short remaining time on mortal politics. Recognizing that his worsening rage could provoke disaster in the capital, he leaves the watcher and fire cultivator with supplies. Falling Leaf joins him as he turns west into the wilds, seeking a violent confrontation that might show him how to master his anger.

Sen and Falling Leaf fight increasingly dangerous spirit beasts, but combat only drains his anger temporarily. After spirit oxen shelter him while a severe leg wound heals, their herd mother directs him toward a barren western region where he may find resolution or death. There an overwhelmingly powerful wind dragon traps the pair and forces Sen into an impossible battle. Sen unleashes his rage in a desperate final attack and survives. Within the dragon's mind, he learns that his anger, paranoia, and self-destructive impulses formed a heart demon. The ordeal has purged it, and the dragon chose not to kill him once it was gone. The dragon confirms that Sen's incomplete body transformation remains fatal and cannot supply the missing instruction. Sen therefore survives his immediate inner crisis with greater calm, but the search for the manual is still urgent.

Sen and Falling Leaf return to the waiting party, and the journey to the capital resumes. Sen establishes conditional trust with Feng's watcher and gives the reluctant fire cultivator a choice between leaving and genuinely training. The man stays, improves under daily instruction, and becomes a more useful companion. The Clear Spring cultivator explains that her family arranged an unwanted marriage and proposes Sen as a more advantageous alternative. Near the capital, she admits that she cannot guarantee the manual and would rather kill the groom than submit. Sen still agrees to help if she commits every available family resource to his search, with a three-month limit. At the southern gate, officials reveal that she is a princess. Sen has now entered the mortal politics he hoped to avoid, using a public courtship strategy to oppose her forced marriage while seeking the manual that may save his life.

The princess's brother approaches Sen after a diviner warns that Sen could bring fortune or disaster. The prince supports ending her arranged marriage to Choi Zhi Peng and begins teaching Sen about the capital's political balance. House Choi is a great-house rival of the throne, making any direct move dangerous. Meanwhile, Steel Griffin cultivators try to seize Falling Leaf as leverage. She and Sen kill the attackers, but Sen initially avoids blaming the whole sect. When an elder later attempts to intimidate them, he wounds and detains her. A nascent-soul Steel Griffin leader intervenes and accepts the elder's loss of assets and a century of confinement. The leader is Feng's brother and agrees to contain the dispute. The prince also commits to helping with the manual. Sen has gained political allies and avoided a sect war, but his alliance with the princess has made Falling Leaf and the rest of his group targets.

Weeks pass while Sen waits for progress on the manual and trains his fire cultivator companion. During meditation on his unusual Heavenly Shadow cultivation, Sen unconsciously draws upon stored cores and forms a second core layer. Four cultivators attack during the advancement, but he maintains a defensive vortex, completes the breakthrough, and kills them. Their markings identify them as members of the Shadow Eagle Talon Syndicate, a criminal organization hired by an unknown patron. Further attacks follow. Sen stops evading the organization, interrogates a poisoned-crossbow assassin, and orders the Syndicate to leave the city. He publicly embraces the name Judgment's Gale as part of that threat. The manual search remains stalled, while Sen's abnormal advancement and open campaign introduce a new capital enemy whose employer is still unknown.

Sen and Feng's watcher cooperate against more Syndicate attackers, narrowly escaping a destructive assault by the organization's bearded nascent-soul head. Senior city cultivators then forbid that leader from personally killing Sen. Sen raids Syndicate properties under concealment, kills its personnel, strips its resources, and returns identifiable stolen goods. Most of House Choi is then massacred by a single powerful cultivator. Sen and the prince suspect the Syndicate head retaliated against the family for initiating the conflict. Choi Zhi Peng survives, and the king still orders the princess's wedding to proceed. Sen meets the Golden Phoenix matriarch, beginning a temporary intimate relationship, but she confirms that her sect no longer has the Five-Fold Body Transformation Manual. The principal capital lead has failed. Sen resolves to eliminate the Syndicate and end the forced-marriage crisis before leaving to pursue the manual elsewhere.

After preparing in secret, Sen infiltrates the Syndicate's concealed cache, kills its guards, and plants a linked array of custom poisons. He deliberately summons the nascent-soul leader into the trap and destroys the man's qi channels before killing him. Sen conceals the method even from the senior cultivators who arrive afterward, while the Golden Phoenix matriarch agrees to push the surviving Syndicate members out of crime or out of the city. The organization is effectively broken. Before killing its leader, Sen voices his belief that he may be accelerated toward ascension to serve an unknown power. He has removed the immediate criminal threat to his companions, but the patron behind the original contract remains unidentified and the deeper cause of his abnormal cultivation is still open.

Feng's watcher and Falling Leaf abduct Choi Zhi Peng and free a child held in his secret torture room. Under interrogation, Choi reveals why the king insists on the marriage: House Choi has evidence that the king trafficked people to demonic cultivators and abused and murdered boys. Sen condemns Choi to die sealed in a stone pit, ending him as a prospective husband. Sen then enters the palace, subdues the guards, and forces the king to confess publicly. The princess's brother kills his father and then kills a rival brother who attacks him for the throne. At the princess's plea, he spares their mother and orders her imprisoned for knowing of the king's crimes. The prince becomes the apparent new ruler. The succession is decided, but the royal family is shattered.

The new king accepts the need for his father's removal but remains angry with Sen and does not banish him. The princess confronts Sen over the deaths and rejects him after his anger turns their dispute cruel, even though the forced marriage is over. Sen recognizes that purging his heart demon did not make his anger harmless. He apologizes to Feng's watcher for his earlier self-righteousness and releases her from Feng's assignment. She stays in the capital with the improving fire cultivator, the fortified house, and Sen's carefully prepared elixir for his advancement. Sen quietly secures support for the new king from the Golden Phoenix matriarch and another nascent-soul cultivator. Falling Leaf chooses to accompany Sen despite the danger. Together they leave for the northwestern wilderness to seek a mad nascent-soul cultivator who may possess the last credible lead to the Five-Fold Body Transformation Manual. Sen's fatal cultivation problem and the force behind his abnormal progress remain unresolved.

characters.description: A homeless boy in Orchard's Reach who steals food to survive and shares what he has with Grandmother Lu. He has no family or reliable shelter, but he is resourceful enough to evade local nobles and remains devoted to the one person who cares for him.
characters.name: Sen

characters.description: Sen's elderly benefactor and only reliable familial comfort. Though poor herself, she shares food and occasional shelter with him.
characters.name: Grandmother Lu

characters.description: A formidable outside cultivator whose presence weighs heavily on the people of Orchard's Reach. He notices Sen despite the boy's hiding place.
characters.name: Feng

characters.name: Kho Jaw-Long

characters.name: Senior household servant

characters.name: Lynn

characters.name: Mayor's son's teacher

characters.name: Surviving hired cultivator

recaps.ending: The mayor's attempt to kill Grandmother Lu and her household ends Sen's willingness to leave the Orchard's Reach feud unresolved. With Falling Leaf, he infiltrates the mayor's estate, incapacitates its guards and workers, and kills the mayor and Jiang Hao. Falling Leaf kills the mayor's wife after judging her denial of involvement false. Grandmother Lu survives with her company, staff, fighting fans, possible advancement medicine, and the gold Sen gives her. She later separates from Sen's eastbound caravan to travel south. Falling Leaf returns to the mountain because human society remains dangerous for her, though she intends to watch over Grandmother Lu at times and may reunite with Sen. Feng and Kho remain behind to investigate the mountain's abnormal spirit-beast violence, while Caihong expects Sen to write. Sen defeats a powerful metal-attuned spirit beast while guarding the caravan, treats his own wounds, and reaches the eastern city connected to the call he has sensed. Its purpose is still unknown. He also continues to owe Laughing River a favor, may face retaliation from a slain cultivator's clan, and expects the freed indebted fighter to meet him on the road.
recaps.in_short: Sen begins as a homeless boy in Orchard's Reach, protected only by Grandmother Lu. The cultivator Feng Ming chooses him as a disciple and takes him to Kho Jaw-Long's mountain home, where Feng, Kho, Ma Caihong, and the spirit beast Falling Leaf become his adopted family and teachers. Years of martial, medical, and cultivation training carry Sen into middle Foundation Formation, but also expose him to the violence of the Jianghu. He returns home before following an unexplained pull toward the east and finds Grandmother Lu restored to health and prosperous. The mayor's family escalates an old grievance into repeated murder attempts. Sen and Falling Leaf kill the mayor, his wife, and Jiang Hao while sparing uninvolved workers. Falling Leaf returns to the mountain, Grandmother Lu turns south with her caravan, and Sen travels east as a guard. After surviving one final spirit-beast attack, he reaches the city that has been calling him.

recaps.text: Sen survives on the streets of Orchard's Reach by stealing and scavenging, sharing what he can with Grandmother Lu, the only person he considers family. When the visiting cultivator Feng announces that he will choose a local disciple, the mayor excludes poor children and presents favored youths instead. Feng discovers Sen in hiding, selects him, and punishes the mayor. Because the rejected nobles may kill Sen after such a humiliation, Feng insists that the boy cannot remain in town. Sen agrees to leave only after Feng gives Grandmother Lu a secure home, money, and medicine. She formally claims Sen as family and gives him the name Lu Sen. On the mountain journey, Feng learns that his new disciple needs ordinary meals and adjusts his pace and route. Sen also befriends a camouflaging Ghost Panther by sharing food with her. Feng promises that Sen will not be punished for voicing necessary concerns. He then gives Sen a pill that begins an agonizing purification of his body.

The purification leaves Sen leaner, stronger, and able to sense energy-rich food. He keeps pace more easily and glimpses the wider world from the mountainside before reaching a secluded manor. Its airborne defender proves to be Feng's old friend Kho Jaw-Long, who welcomes Sen as a nephew. Kho identifies the boy's earlier cleansing as an earthly transformation and confirms that Sen possesses an unusual ability to hide his presence. Once Sen admits that he cannot read, Kho undertakes his education and also teaches him basic cooking. Feng handles self-defense and physical conditioning. Across the seasons, Sen develops literacy, endurance, strikes, blocks, and controlled martial forms, while the Ghost Panther runs beside him and becomes a steady companion. By the next New Year, Sen can read independently, prepare meals, and perform Feng's foundational form with enough precision to stop a blow just short of his master. Feng releases him from close supervision of the basics. Kho gives him a spear, Feng gives him a straight sword, and Sen accepts a second cleansing pill as his training moves into more dangerous territory.

Sen uses the second cleansing to open more internal channels, leaving his energy reserve depleted. While he recovers, Kho's history lessons show him that neither ordinary society nor cultivation offers complete safety. The Ghost Panther guides him toward the power gathered near his navel. Sen secretly experiments with it, learning to circulate it but not how to replenish it. During a severe training drill, Feng exhausts that reserve and finally recognizes the misunderstanding. He identifies it as Sen's lower dantian, names its energy qi, and teaches him to draw power from the world before lasting damage occurs. Feng accepts responsibility for withholding foundational knowledge, while Sen admits that embarrassment led him to conceal his experiments. Two more years pass. Sen cultivates while moving, learns that qi has varied attributes, and develops access to an exceptionally broad range, with fire and shadow his strongest affinities. Feng requires him to train the weaker ones as well. The Ghost Panther reveals her name as Falling Leaf. With Sen's basic cultivation established, Feng announces that the next task is developing killing intent.

Feng demonstrates killing intent by overwhelming Sen without touching him, then proposes sending him across the mountain to acquire it through real danger. Kho strongly objects, and his wife Ma Caihong arrives to demand an independent assessment. Her argument with Feng exposes an old grievance but not its cause. Caihong tests Sen's sword work, patience, qi techniques, and concealment, then helps equip him with medicine and a storage ring. Feng kills many of the mountain's strongest spirit beasts before the trial, an act intended to improve Sen's odds. Sen sets out for a cave on the far side, and Falling Leaf follows. He kills attacking spirit beasts, discovers that Caihong's treatment opened previously blocked channels, and begins combining qi techniques despite the strain. Falling Leaf saves him from a falling hawk and guards him while he heals. Over several days their combat routine sharpens his weaker affinities and fills his ring with beast cores. When a white ape strikes Falling Leaf down, Sen believes she has been killed. His desire to avenge her finally forms killing intent, which he combines with fire qi to kill the ape.

Falling Leaf survives the ape's blow. Sen tends her with Caihong's emergency medicine, learns to direct his new killing intent, and completes the mountain crossing. Feng is troubled that normally cautious spirit beasts attacked so aggressively and accepts responsibility for investigating. Back at the manor, Sen reconciles with Caihong and accepts her lessons in medicine, field remedies, sword misdirection, and control of killing intent. He begins calling her Auntie Caihong, and that recognition of family triggers a major breakthrough. Sen condenses his first liquid qi and simultaneously completes qi condensation and earthly transformation, entering Foundation Formation in both spirit and body cultivation. His teachers finally explain the formal stages and their own specialties: Feng centers on combat, Caihong on healing and alchemy, and Kho on formations. During further field study, Sen meets the red spirit fox Laughing River. She trades a rare blossom for his promise of a future favor and sends greetings to Caihong. Falling Leaf also reveals that she can speak through qi. At New Year, Sen delivers the flower and message, while his teachers give him a preservation ring, a liquid-qi manual, and durable writing tools for his eventual travels.

Caihong judges Sen capable of emergency stabilization but not a spirit doctor. Kho begins teaching him the spear and formations, emphasizing balance and changing conditions. Sen adopts a foundation method that condenses all the qi attributes he can use rather than forcing him into one specialty. His body and qi reserves strengthen, and he considers several possible paths without choosing one. The mountain's abnormal spirit-beast behavior remains under investigation. When three core formation cultivators pursue Feng home and threaten Sen, Kho kills two and sends the survivor back to the Diving Falcon Sect with a warning. The incident forces Sen's teachers to explain the Jianghu, the informal world of cultivator reputation, challenges, controlled violence, and feuds. Feng's reputation attracts conflict, while guest obligations required Kho to answer a threat against Sen. Each elder explains why cultivation once appealed to them, but none can promise that violence is avoidable. Falling Leaf tells Sen that he will fight when forced, just as an animal defends itself. Sen decides not to abandon cultivation. Instead, he asks for realistic preparation against wounds, ambushes, groups, and situations where escape matters more than victory.

Months of harsh group combat teach Sen to function through pain, exhaustion, distraction, and attacks from several directions. He improves his spiritual awareness, accepts healing pills when necessary, and learns to maintain several qi patterns at once. During this period he senses an unexplained call from the east that seems connected to the ocean. He decides to leave in spring, first visiting Grandmother Lu and then seeking a practical route east. Feng, Kho, and Caihong affirm that the manor remains his home while preparing him for independence with contacts, travel warnings, lightning qi, spear refinement, and qinggong. Falling Leaf refuses his invitation to accompany him because humans would hunt her, but leaves open the possibility of meeting again. Another breakthrough carries Sen to middle Foundation Formation. His teachers give him travel robes, a map, a spirit-level sword, money, medicine, and other supplies. Caihong includes a sealed preparation for a future attempt at core formation, and Kho sends a package to Grandmother Lu. Sen finally departs the mountain for Orchard's Reach. Feng and Kho remain behind to investigate the spirit-beast disturbance, while Feng quietly arranges for others to watch over his disciple from a distance.

Sen and Falling Leaf part at the forest edge, and he enters Orchard's Reach while concealing his strength. Grandmother Lu now has servants and a large, successful trading company. She appears decades younger because Feng's medicine repaired meridians damaged by her cultivator family in childhood and restored her ability to cycle qi. After being discarded by that family, she lived as a mortal and later fell into poverty. She built the new business with Feng's money and her restored health so Sen would have support across the region. Jiang Hao soon confronts Sen with six qi-condensing associates. Sen defeats the attackers without killing them. A large unarmed cultivator refuses to join the assault because he serves only under a family debt. Sen promises to arrange the payment through Grandmother Lu so the man can become a wanderer. Reflecting on the public fear caused by his strength, Sen resolves to use power for protection rather than indulgence. The insight triggers a breakthrough. He reaches Grandmother Lu's home and takes the dangerous opportunity to stretch his dantian and channels, using a self-made elixir to reinforce them. The alteration greatly expands his possible qi flow, though its cost is not yet clear.

Sen wakes with wider channels and a larger dantian, but his existing qi now fills only part of the expanded space. He uses a formation and spirit-beast cores to accelerate recovery, drawing on lessons from Kho and Caihong. Grandmother Lu helps sell ordinary cores discreetly and completes the payment that frees the indebted fighter. A Foundation Formation blade cultivator, Jiang Hao's teacher, then demands a death duel in the market. Sen fights cautiously until the man threatens Grandmother Lu's employees. Sen answers with killing intent and kills him, then takes his weapons, money, seal, and concealed storage ring as spoils. He publicly directs suspicion toward the mayor, hoping to weaken the family without an immediate assault. The captured ring contains valuable equipment and a large quantity of gold that Grandmother Lu believes belongs to the mayor. She expects its loss to provoke violence that very night. Sen gives her pills from Feng and Caihong that may permit a breakthrough to Foundation Formation, as well as Kho's gift of sharpened fighting fans suited to her old training. Returning the gold will not ensure safety, so they prepare for an attack.

Sen waits at Grandmother Lu's shop behind an alarm formation and detects five intruders. Using concealing shadows, he kills most of the attackers and captures a surviving Foundation Formation cultivator, who identifies the mayor as their employer. Sen pays her to leave town and warns her never to return or threaten Grandmother Lu. He then discovers that a second group has attacked the house. Falling Leaf has returned and protects the injured senior servant, while Grandmother Lu defends the maid. Sen kills three assailants and Grandmother Lu defeats the last. After stabilizing the servant with an elixir, Sen decides the mayor must die. Grandmother Lu agrees but insists that guards, servants, and other uninvolved people must be spared. Sen and Falling Leaf enter the mayor's estate under cover of shadow, disabling guards and sedating workers rather than treating everyone present as an enemy. Sen confronts and kills the mayor. Falling Leaf kills the mayor's wife after judging her claim of ignorance false, and Sen kills Jiang Hao when he promises lifelong revenge. The mayor's immediate family is dead, while most estate workers remain alive.

With the feud ended, Sen accepts that Orchard's Reach no longer holds him. Falling Leaf returns to the mountain because remaining among humans would expose her to hunters, though she agrees to check on Grandmother Lu from time to time. Sen gives Grandmother Lu enough gold for lasting security and joins her eastbound caravan as a guard. The mayor's death has destabilized local government, but the guards do not attempt to arrest a wandering cultivator they cannot practically control. Before departure, Sen proves his value to the caravan's body-cultivator captain and obtains a favored bun recipe from a local family. Grandmother Lu plans to turn south with the caravan, while Sen continues east toward the unexplained pull he has sensed for months. On the road, a powerful metal-attuned spirit beast attacks. Sen kills it with an improvised lightning-infused spear strike, sustaining multiple wounds in the explosion. His medical training lets him treat himself and recover during the remainder of the journey. He finally arrives at the eastern city that has been calling him, independent and well supplied, with the purpose of that summons still unknown.

recaps.ending: Sen leaves for the capital to honor the king's summons, accompanied by Glimmer of Night in human form and an unidentified human companion. Liu Ai remains behind after calling Sen Papa for the first time. Falling Leaf, Kho, and Caihong accept responsibility for her safety. Wu Meng Yao takes charge of the academy, and Kho will cover its lower-level spear instruction. The academy is functioning and the town can now mount an organized defense, but its staffing and relations with nearby sects remain unsettled. The lightning sect may retaliate for its leader's death. Falling Leaf still cannot regain her Ghost Panther form, Laughing River's fox purge and ascension remain unresolved, and the spirit-beast king has only been warned off. Sen can enter the Shadow Realm, though divine qi and unsafe exits make the technique potentially lethal. He also has not decided how far he will support the king politically, and the role awaiting him in the capital is unknown.
recaps.in_short: Sen settles near a vulnerable town while caring for the orphaned Liu Ai, repairing his relationship with Falling Leaf, and learning shadow cultivation from a nascent-soul instructor. His efforts to prepare mortals for spirit-beast attacks grow into an inclusive weapons academy for mortals and cultivators. The town survives a bearcat assault, and Sen recruits instructors while powerful elders help stabilize his household. He eventually enters the Shadow Realm, but divine qi makes the technique unusually dangerous. When lightning-sect cultivators attempt to inspect the academy, Sen kills their leader and expels the survivors. Elsewhere, Laughing River begins a violent purge among the foxes, while Feng Ming crushes a spirit-beast army and warns its king to end attacks on humans. At the close, Liu Ai calls Sen Papa. Sen leaves her with Falling Leaf, Kho, and Caihong, places Wu Meng Yao in charge of the academy, and departs for the capital with Glimmer of Night and a human companion.

recaps.text: Previously: Sen became a powerful wandering cultivator with close ties to Falling Leaf and formidable allies including Feng, Kho, and Caihong. He acquired the epithet Judgment's Gale and survived a confrontation with a true devil, though he cannot be certain that enemy was destroyed. His travels also created obligations to the nine-tailed fox Laughing River and brought him into contact with Laughing River's granddaughter, Misty Peak. The possible survival of the devil remains unresolved as this volume begins.

Sen reunites Falling Leaf with the foxes Laughing River and Misty Peak, then pauses his own concerns to save a logger trapped beneath a tree. His return to the inn reveals that Falling Leaf has violently repelled men who tried to seize her. Sen is also struggling with responsibility for an orphaned girl, assisted by Glimmer of Night and a nascent-soul cultivator who begins teaching him shadow travel. When Falling Leaf disappears with Laughing River, Sen's anger becomes dangerous enough to threaten the child he means to protect. He restrains himself, and Falling Leaf soon returns. Laughing River explains that he tried and failed to restore her Ghost Panther form because an unknown force blocks the transformation. Sen gives him the spatial treasure required for his overdue ascension but condemns taking Falling Leaf without warning. Laughing River departs with the treasure, leaving their trust damaged and Falling Leaf's condition unexplained.

Falling Leaf challenges Sen's attempt to control her choices, and their serious fight forces him to acknowledge that fear does not justify denying her independence. Soon afterward, spirit beasts attack the nearby town. Sen organizes mortal defenders instead of doing everything himself, kills the strongest beast, treats the wounded, and encourages the town to buy proper weapons with the beast cores. The attack appears connected to wider abnormal spirit-beast activity. As he studies shadow qi, Glimmer of Night's inherited web patterns give Sen new ideas, and his instructor helps him develop stable, self-sustaining shadow constructs. Meanwhile, Sen teaches the orphaned girl and Glimmer of Night to write. Townspeople ask him for weapons training, so he reluctantly creates a training yard and pushes a veteran former soldier toward local leadership. He also repairs his friendship with Falling Leaf by making time for her and inviting her into the child's daily life. Shadow walking itself remains beyond him.

The orphaned girl is now identified as Liu Ai. Sen makes the training hall explicitly open to women, men, and children, appoints the veteran spear instructor as its mortal leader, and continues improving both the facility and its students. Two cultivators arrive, one at core formation and one at foundation formation. The core cultivator seeks to repay a perceived debt to Sen, but he initially invents a hazardous treasure quest to make her leave. Before that plan can unfold, six bearcats attack. The mortal teams use their training to kill all six without fatalities, although Sen and the visitors intervene to prevent several deaths. Glimmer of Night then supplies the layered-reality model that lets Sen understand the basis of shadow walking. The nascent-soul instructor admits her uncontrolled killing intent may endanger Liu Ai, so Sen decides the child can no longer stay at her residence. Elsewhere, Caihong and Jaw-Long set out after receiving Sen's letter, while Laughing River begins executing foxes he considers traitors and moves toward Emperor's Bay.

Growing cultivator interest forces Sen to decide what his training project should become. Caihong and Kho arrive, bringing practical support and powerful attention. Kho assesses the mortal trainees, while Sen recognizes that control over armed townspeople could make him look like a local ruler. He rejects both that path and the obligations of a sect, choosing instead to found a weapons academy for mortals and cultivators. Its rules prohibit abuse of mortals, keep cultivation instruction outside its mission, and allow useful service to offset high cultivator fees. Sen abandons the fictitious mountain quest and persuades the core-formation visitor to become a sword instructor. He also promises tailored advancement help to her foundation-formation companion. The academy's first cultivator applicants test its standards: Sen forces one man to apologize for belittling a weaker woman and offers that woman guidance for a breakthrough. A pale, blue-eyed core cultivator also seeks Sen as both teacher and companion, but Falling Leaf recognizes her possessive agenda and Sen rejects it.

The academy becomes a lasting institution with an inclusive admissions policy, mortal literacy and physical training, and a climate formation installed by Kho. A royal messenger summons Sen to a court gathering, and Sen chooses the foundation-formation visitor as his companion for the trip. His shadow training finally succeeds when he suppresses the divine qi embedded in his skin and enters the Shadow Realm. Repeated practice proves that the technique is usable, but overstaying or choosing a poor exit can kill him, and his divine qi makes every transition harder. Before he can leave, three cultivators from a lightning-marked sect arrive and claim the right to inspect the academy. Their leader has a past relationship with the resident sword instructor. When one companion admits the inspection's purpose, Sen makes him acknowledge that a sect would treat the same intrusion as a capital offense. Sen kills the leader and expels the other two, leaving the sect's authorization and likely response uncertain.

Sen claims the dead sect leader's treasures and explains the confrontation to the mortal students, but their new fear of him exposes a social distance he cannot remove. Falling Leaf convinces him that respectful caution may protect mortals in future encounters with cultivators. Sen then prepares the academy for his absence. Kho agrees to teach lower-level spear students and tells Sen that his own next spear form must be personally created. The resident sword instructor receives authority over the academy, while other cultivator students are ordered to follow her direction. Caihong warns that the king may try to use Sen's power, prompting him to consider limits on what friendship requires. Elsewhere, Li Yi Nuo reaches Orchard's Reach seeking someone connected to Sen's spear training, only to learn that the contact has gone west. Feng Ming kills an ancient dragon, destroys a gathered spirit-beast force, and releases a serpent envoy with an ultimatum for its king: stop attacks on human settlements or face war with human cultivators.

Sen confirms that Wu Meng Yao is an effective sword instructor and publicly entrusts the academy to her. At a final household gathering, Glimmer of Night reveals that he has learned to assume the appearance of a young human man and asks to join the capital journey. Kho and Caihong also explain that Sen's repeated refusal of advances from Laughing River's granddaughter carries an unintended courtship meaning among the foxes. Sen refuses to bring Liu Ai into the dangers of the capital and assures her that Falling Leaf, Kho, and Caihong will keep her safe. Liu Ai calls him Papa for the first time. Despite Fu Ru Lan's warning, Sen chooses to honor his promise to the king, who has an unspecified role planned for him. He leaves for the capital with Glimmer of Night and a human companion. The academy continues under Wu Meng Yao, but the fox conflict, spirit-beast campaign, sect consequences, Falling Leaf's blocked transformation, and Sen's hazardous shadow cultivation all remain open.

characters.description: An independent cultivator travelling by sea and accepted by the ship's crew. He places their safety above his own when a powerful sea spirit beast threatens the vessel. Sen intends to meet his existing obligations before attempting a much longer journey across the continent.
characters.name: Sen

After her sect's specialists fail to help them, a hostile elder assigns her the dangerous task of finding the cultivator responsible and bringing that person back.
characters.name: Li Yi Nuo

characters.name: Hostile sect elder

characters.description: The returning captain of the ship carrying Sen. He values reaching his family safely over voyages that could keep his crew away from home for years, and he discusses those risks with Sen as a sea spirit beast approaches.
characters.name: Ship captain

characters.name: Li Yi Nuo's master

He explains that Sen's exposure to divine qi has altered the intended process into an unpredictable six-fold transformation, though he cannot say what its final effects will be.
